subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on Land Rover engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the AJ-V8 across its Land Rover applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The AJ-V8 in the Range Rover Sport L320 is the primary application we work on for this engine family. The 4.2-litre supercharged variant is the one that tends to come through our workshop most frequently, though we also see naturally aspirated 4.4-litre examples.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Timing chain, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every rebuild, with supercharger components inspected and serviced where fitted.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: Timing chain tensioner wear is documented on higher-mileage examples. Valve seal deterioration can lead to increased oil consumption. On supercharged variants, the supercharger coupler can wear over time, causing rattling or whining noises. Early engines (1998-2002) had Nikasil cylinder lining issues caused by reaction with high-sulphur fuel, but this is less relevant to L320 applications (2005-2013) as the issue was addressed.

typical.title: LAND ROVER AJ-V8 REBUILD
typical.intro: The following describes a typical rebuild scope for this engine — illustrative of the work involved, not a specific customer job. Real case studies from our own completed work will replace this section once available.
typical.body: The AJ-V8's timing chain system uses a conventional front-mounted chain arrangement, with tensioners and guides that wear over time. On higher-mileage examples, the timing chain tensioners can lose tension, creating a rattling noise on cold start that usually goes away as oil pressure builds. Over time, the aluminium guide rails (on early examples) and tensioner wear can lead to chain slack and, if left unaddressed, more significant engine damage. On supercharged variants, the supercharger coupler is a known wear item — a rubber isolator within the supercharger drive that can break down over time, creating a characteristic rattling or whining noise from the supercharger area. The supercharger itself is also inspected for bearing wear, as the additional load on the engine and the heat generated by forced induction puts more stress on certain components.

scope.label: Typical Scope:
scope.text: Timing chain, bearings, gaskets, valve seals, supercharger coupler (where applicable), supercharger inspection (where applicable)
